newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israelis protest Netanyahu, Palestinians besieged.
newsitem.headline: Israelis protest Netanyahu, Palestinians besieged.

text.p: Tens of thousands of Israeli peace activists took to the streets but Palestinians were confined to their towns as Yasser Arafat and Benjamin Netanyahu held marathon talks at an emergency summit in Washington.

"There is no light at the end of that tunnel," chanted Israeli activists at a Tel Aviv peace rally, referring to an archaeological tunnel near Islamic shrines in Jerusalem whose opening sparked bloody clashes which killed 57 Palestinians and 15 Israelis last week.

Netanyahu's decision to open a second entrance to the tunnel in Old Jerusalem's Moslem Quarter triggered the violence. The clashes prompted U.S. President Bill Clinton to call Palestinian President Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu to the summit to deal with the crisis.
In the West Bank, tightened Israeli travel restrictions on Palestinians imposed during the clashes began to bite.

In the southern West Bank town of Hebron, an 18-month-old baby with leukaemia who was being rushed to a Jerusalem hospital for a blood transfusion died after Israeli soldiers delayed him for an hour at a roadblock, human rights groups said.
Israel barred most Palestinians from travelling between self-ruled enclaves in the West Bank after declaring the territory a closed military area.
Israeli troops ringed Palestinian cities with tanks and armoured vehicles and set up barricades on main roads, cutting links between 450 communities.
Palestinians say the closure has kept thousands of Arabs stranded away from home, stifled their economy and threatened to deprive them of health services.

"Human rights groups and non-govermental organisations express deep concern over the deteriorating human rights conditions in the occupied Palestinian territories," said a statement issued by eight groups.
An Israeli army spokeswoman insisted Palestinian humanitarian needs were being handled through joint Israeli-PLO liaison channels.

In Nablus, where the closure was enforced by about 45 tanks pointing their guns at the city of 130,000, Palestinians said factories were working at only 30 percent capacity because workers from surrounding villages could not get to their jobs.
Witnesses said on Tuesday that Palestinian police had dug trenches opposite Israeli armour around Nablus in preparation for a possible resumption of violence if the Washington summit fails.
Some 50,000 Israeli peace activists demonstrated in Tel Aviv against the violence and Netanyahu's policies.

"We want the government of Israel to implement the agreement which it has not implemented in the last three months. If this happens we will be back on track. If not we will be in the streets," said Yossi Beilin, a Labour party architect of the Oslo peace accords which led to Palestinian self-rule.
"We can prove to ourselves and the world that the peace is stronger than its opponents," Beilin told the rally.
